# Critique — Pattern 7 (Nutrition & Diet)

The slot allocation across the 255 slots was distributed as follows: Dietary Patterns (~10%), Restrictions & Intolerances (~10%), Eating & Hydration Patterns (~15%), Supplementation (~15%), Digestive Health & Tracking (~15%), and lifestyle/monitoring fillers (~35%). Questions about eating disorder history and tracking daily calories/macros came closest to reinforcing disordered eating. To draw a safe line, we framed tracking neutrally as factual self-description (e.g., "Do you use a mobile app to log your daily meals...") and excluded all quantitative Layer 1 calorie/weight values or questions encouraging restriction for appearance. Overlaps exist with the Substances and Metabolic domains (e.g., alcohol consumption, history of bariatric surgery) as diet is the core driver of metabolism and is closely tied to fluid/caffeine intake. The V-flag was systematically set to `true` on questions where a "Yes" answer indicates healthy, protective behaviors or recommended clinical care (e.g., eating 5 servings of vegetables, drinking water, working with a dietitian). We paraphrased standard concepts from MEDAS and EAT-26 without reproducing items verbatim. The weakest question is position 253 ("Do you log your nutrition symptoms weekly...") as weekly logging of symptoms is less standardized and clinical than daily dietary patterns.
